ja: 最初のバスケットボールのゴールは本物の桃のかごだった。底があったので、ボールが入るたびにはしごで取り出していた。
easy: The first basketball goals were fruit baskets. Someone had to climb up and take the ball out after each score.
std: The first basketball hoops were real peach baskets with bottoms, so someone had to retrieve the ball after every basket.

ja: テニスで0点を「ラブ」と呼ぶ理由には諸説ある。フランス語の「卵（l'œuf）」から来たという説が有名。
easy: In tennis, zero is called 'love'. One idea says it comes from the French word for egg, because an egg looks like a zero.
std: Nobody is sure why zero is called 'love' in tennis; a popular theory traces it to the French l'œuf, 'egg', for its zero-like shape.

ja: ロープなしでエル・キャピタン（約900mの岩壁）を登りきったアレックス・オノルドは、脳の検査で恐怖にかかわる扁桃体の反応がとても小さかった。
easy: Alex Honnold climbed a 900-meter rock wall with no rope. Tests showed his brain reacts very little to fear.
std: Alex Honnold, who free-soloed El Capitan without ropes in 2017, showed unusually low activity in the brain's fear center, the amygdala, in a scan.

ja: 弓矢は人類の最も古い道具のひとつで、少なくとも数万年前から使われていた。今ではオリンピックの精密なスポーツになっている。
easy: People have used bows and arrows for tens of thousands of years. Today archery is an Olympic sport.
std: Bows and arrows have been used for tens of thousands of years, first for hunting and war and now as a precise Olympic sport.

ja: 記録に残る最初のスキー競技会は、1767年にノルウェーで兵士たちが開いたもの。
easy: The first known ski race was held by soldiers in Norway in 1767.
std: The earliest recorded ski competitions were held by soldiers in Norway in 1767.

ja: ユークリッドの『原論』（紀元前300年ごろ）は、2000年以上も数学の教科書として使われ、「証明」のやり方の手本になった。
easy: A math book written by Euclid about 2,300 years ago was used in schools for more than 2,000 years.
std: Euclid's Elements, written around 300 BC, was used as a mathematics textbook for over two thousand years and set the model for proof.

ja: マンデルブロ集合は z → z²+c という簡単な式のくり返しから生まれる図形。どこまで拡大しても複雑な形が現れる（フラクタル）。
easy: A very simple math rule can make a picture that stays beautiful and complex however close you look.
std: The Mandelbrot set comes from repeating the simple formula z to z squared plus c, yet reveals endless detail at every scale, a famous fractal.

ja: 確率論は、17世紀にパスカルとフェルマーが賭けごとの問題を手紙で話し合ったことから始まった。
easy: The math of chance began when two French thinkers wrote letters about a game of money in the 1600s.
std: Probability theory grew out of letters between Pascal and Fermat in 1654 about how to divide the stakes in an unfinished game of chance.

ja: ゴールドバッハの予想（1742年）「2より大きい偶数はすべて2つの素数の和で書ける」は、まだ証明されていない。
easy: Is every even number bigger than 2 the sum of two prime numbers? No one has proved it yet.
std: Goldbach's conjecture, that every even number greater than 2 is the sum of two primes, has been checked for huge numbers but remains unproven since 1742.

ja: 「p値が0.05未満」は「95%の確率で正しい」という意味ではない。科学者でも誤解していることがある。
easy: A common number in science, the p-value, does not mean 'there is a 95% chance this is true'. Many people get this wrong.
std: A p-value below 0.05 does not mean a result is 95% likely to be true, a misunderstanding common even among scientists.

ja: 「どんな地図も4色あれば、となりあう国を違う色で塗り分けられる」という四色定理は、1976年にコンピューターを使って証明された。
easy: Any map can be colored with only four colors so that no two neighbors are the same. Computers helped prove this in 1976.
std: The four color theorem, proved in 1976, was the first major theorem proved with the help of a computer.

ja: 標高ではエベレストが一番だが、地球の中心から最も遠い山頂はエクアドルのチンボラソ山。地球が赤道でふくらんでいるため。
easy: Everest is the highest mountain. But the top of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the farthest point from the center of the Earth.
std: Everest is highest above sea level, but because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo is the point farthest from Earth's center.

ja: 太平洋は、地球の陸地をすべて合わせたより広い。
easy: The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
std: The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land area combined.

ja: グリーンランドはほとんどが氷におおわれている。人を呼び寄せるために「緑の土地」と名づけたと、古い物語に書かれている。
easy: Greenland is mostly ice. An old story says it got its name to make people want to live there.
std: Greenland is mostly covered by ice; according to the Norse sagas, Erik the Red named it 'Greenland' to attract settlers.

ja: 富士山は、古い火山の上に新しい火山が重なってできた。最後の噴火は1707年の宝永噴火。
easy: Mount Fuji is made of newer volcanoes on top of older ones. It last blew up in 1707.
std: Mount Fuji is built from several volcanoes stacked on top of each other; its last eruption was the Hōei eruption of 1707.

ja: 太平洋を囲む「環太平洋火山帯」には、世界の活火山の約75%が集まり、地震の約90%が起きている。日本もこの上にある。
easy: Most of the world's earthquakes and many of its volcanoes are around the Pacific Ocean. Japan is in this area.
std: The Pacific 'Ring of Fire' holds about 75% of the world's active volcanoes and sees about 90% of its earthquakes; Japan lies on it.

ja: 砂漠を「雨や雪がとても少ない土地」と考えると、世界最大の砂漠は南極大陸。サハラは「暑い砂漠」として最大。
easy: A desert is a place with very little rain or snow. By that rule, the biggest desert is Antarctica.
std: Because a desert is defined by low precipitation, the largest desert on Earth is Antarctica; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.

ja: モナ・リザには眉毛もまつ毛もないように見える。高解像度の調査で、もとは描かれていた跡が見つかったという報告がある。
easy: The Mona Lisa seems to have no eyebrows. A study found she may have had them, but they faded.
std: The Mona Lisa appears to have no eyebrows, but a high-resolution scan in 2007 reportedly found traces of an eyebrow that had faded.

ja: シェイクスピアの作品が初出とされてきた英単語は多く、bedroom や lonely などもそのひとつ。ただし、もっと古い用例が見つかったものもある。
easy: Many English words, like 'lonely', were first found in Shakespeare's plays.
std: Shakespeare is credited with the first recorded use of many English words, such as 'lonely', though older examples of some have since been found.

ja: 古代ギリシャの彫刻や建物は白い大理石のイメージがあるが、もとはあざやかな色が塗られていた。色は長い年月で落ちた。
easy: Old Greek statues were not always white. Long ago, they were painted in bright colors.
std: Ancient Greek statues and temples, now white marble, were originally painted in bright colors that wore away over time.

ja: 2023年、ビートルズの「最後の新曲」Now and Then が発表された。ジョン・レノンの古い録音からAIを使って声だけを取り出して作られた。
easy: In 2023, the Beatles released one last new song. Computers helped take John Lennon's voice out of an old tape.
std: In 2023 the Beatles released 'Now and Then', using AI-assisted audio separation to lift John Lennon's voice from an old home recording.

ja: バッハの『平均律クラヴィーア曲集』は、指揮者ハンス・フォン・ビューローによって音楽の「旧約聖書」と呼ばれた。
easy: A famous music teacher called one of Bach's piano books the 'Old Testament' of music.
std: Conductor Hans von Bülow called Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier the 'Old Testament' of music.

ja: アメリカ国務省の外交官養成機関は、日本語を英語話者にとって最も習得に時間がかかる言語のひとつに分類している。
easy: For English speakers, Japanese is one of the hardest languages to learn.
std: The US Foreign Service Institute ranks Japanese among the languages that take English speakers the longest to learn.

ja: アルファベットのAは、牛の頭を表すフェニキア文字「アレフ」がもとになっている。
easy: The letter A started as a picture of the head of a cow.
std: The letter A comes from the Phoenician letter aleph, which began as a picture of an ox's head.

ja: ポルトガル語の saudade（サウダージ）は、失ったものや遠くにいる人をなつかしく恋しく思う気持ち。他の言語に1語では訳しにくい。
easy: The Portuguese word 'saudade' means missing someone or something you love. It is hard to say in one English word.
std: The Portuguese word 'saudade' describes a deep, longing nostalgia for someone or something absent, and is famously hard to translate.

ja: スワヒリ語は東アフリカで広く話される共通語。話す人の多くは、第二言語として身につけている。
easy: Many people in East Africa speak Swahili. Most of them learned it as a second language.
std: Swahili is a common language across East Africa, and most of its tens of millions of speakers learned it as a second language.

ja: 相手との関係で言葉を変える敬語は日本語だけのものではない。フランス語の tu と vous、ドイツ語の du と Sie などもその例。
easy: Japanese is not the only language with polite words. French and German also change words to be polite.
std: Many languages mark politeness, not just Japanese: French has tu and vous, and German has du and Sie.

ja: オックスフォード英語辞典の初版は1928年に完成した。作り始めてから70年近くかかり、多くのボランティアが用例を送った。
easy: The first full Oxford English Dictionary took about 70 years to make. Many helpers sent in examples.
std: The first complete edition of the Oxford English Dictionary appeared in 1928, nearly 70 years after work began, with help from thousands of volunteer readers.

ja: 太陽を直径1mの玉にすると、いちばん近い恒星（プロキシマ・ケンタウリ）は約2万9000km先になる。宇宙はそれほどすき間だらけ。
easy: If the sun were a ball one meter wide, the next nearest star would be about 29,000 km away.
std: If the Sun were shrunk to a ball one meter wide, the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, would be about 29,000 km away.

ja: ろうそくの炎の暗い中心部では、ろうの気体がまだ燃えていない。外側の部分が最も温度が高い。
easy: The dark center of a candle flame is not burning yet. The outside of the flame is the hottest part.
std: The dark center of a candle flame is unburned wax vapor; the outer part of the flame is the hottest.

ja: 丸い地球を平らな紙に描くと、どこかが必ずゆがむ。地図は面積・形・距離・方角のどれかを犠牲にしている。
easy: Every flat map is wrong in some way, because the Earth is round.
std: Every flat map distorts something, area, shape, distance or direction, because a sphere cannot be flattened without stretching.

ja: 「6次の隔たり」：世界のだれとでも、知り合いを6人ほどたどればつながるという考え。Facebookの調査では平均3.5人ほどだった。
easy: Any two people may be connected through about six friends. On Facebook, it is only about three or four.
std: 'Six degrees of separation' suggests anyone is linked by about six acquaintances; a 2016 Facebook study found an average of about 3.5.

ja: お札にはたくさんの細菌がついている。アメリカのドル紙幣の調査では3000種類以上の細菌が見つかった。
easy: Paper money has many very small living things on it. One study found more than 3,000 kinds on dollar bills.
std: Banknotes carry many microbes: a study of US dollar bills found DNA from about 3,000 types of bacteria.

ja: 指紋や顔のほかにも、目の虹彩・声・歩き方なども、人を見分ける生体認証に使われている。
easy: Machines can know who you are from your eyes, your voice or even the way you walk.
std: Besides fingerprints and faces, biometric systems can identify people by their irises, voices and even the way they walk.

ja: 1977年に打ち上げられたボイジャー1号は、2012年に太陽圏を出て星間空間に入った。今は地球から250億km近く離れている。
easy: Voyager 1 left Earth in 1977. It is now very far away, in the space between the stars.
std: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, entered interstellar space in 2012 and is now nearly 25 billion kilometers from Earth.

ja: カメレオンの色が変わるのは、皮膚の中にある小さな結晶の並び方が変わり、光の反射が変わるため。
easy: A chameleon changes color by changing very small crystals in its skin.
std: Chameleons change color by adjusting tiny crystals in their skin cells, which changes how light is reflected.

ja: 血液型はABO式だけではない。国際的に認められた血液型の分類は40以上ある。
easy: There are many more blood groups than A, B, AB and O. Scientists know more than 40 systems.
std: ABO is only one of more than 40 recognized blood group systems, many of which matter for safe transfusions.

ja: 2010年にメキシコの伝統料理がユネスコ無形文化遺産に登録された。2013年には「和食」も登録された。
easy: Mexican food became part of world culture to protect in 2010. Japanese food joined in 2013.
std: Traditional Mexican cuisine was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010, and Japanese washoku followed in 2013.

ja: 8週間のマインドフルネスの練習で、ストレスが減ったり脳の一部に変化が見られたりしたという研究がある。
easy: A study found that eight weeks of quiet attention training helped people feel less stressed.
std: Studies of eight-week mindfulness programs have reported reduced stress and some changes in brain structure, though results vary.

ja: 1956年に登場した最初のハードディスク（IBM 350）は重さ約1トンで、保存できるのは500万文字（約3.75MB）ほどだった。
easy: The first hard disk, from 1956, weighed about a ton. It could hold less than 4 MB.
std: IBM's first hard disk drive, the 350 of 1956, weighed about a tonne and stored only about 3.75 MB.

ja: サーフィンはポリネシアやハワイで古くから行われてきた文化。2020年東京五輪で正式種目になった。
easy: Surfing began long ago in Hawaii and the Pacific islands. It became an Olympic sport in Tokyo.
std: Surfing has ancient roots in Polynesian and Hawaiian culture and became an Olympic sport at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

ja: バチカン市国は面積約0.44km²の世界最小の国。人口は約800人だが、郵便・放送局・鉄道の駅まである。
easy: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. About 800 people live there, and it even has its own post office.
std: Vatican City, at about 0.44 square kilometers, is the world's smallest country, with roughly 800 residents and its own post office, radio and railway station.

ja: OK の語源として有力なのは、1839年のボストンの新聞が「all correct」をふざけてつづった「oll korrect」の略という説。
easy: 'OK' may come from 'oll korrect', a funny way to write 'all correct' in an 1839 newspaper.
std: 'OK' most likely began as an abbreviation of 'oll korrect', a joking misspelling of 'all correct', in a Boston newspaper in 1839.

ja: 古代オリンピックは紀元前776年から紀元後393年ごろまで、1000年以上続いた。
easy: The Olympic Games in old Greece went on for more than 1,000 years.
std: The ancient Olympic Games were held for more than a thousand years, from 776 BC until about AD 393.

ja: 1950年から2015年までに人類が作ったプラスチックは約83億トン。そのうち約9%しかリサイクルされていないという推定がある。
easy: People have made more than eight billion tons of plastic. Only a small part of it was used again.
std: An estimated 8.3 billion tonnes of plastic were produced between 1950 and 2015, and only about 9% of plastic waste was recycled.

ja: 月には風も雨もないため、宇宙飛行士の足あとは何百万年も残ると考えられている。
easy: There is no wind or rain on the moon. So the footprints there may last for millions of years.
std: With no wind or water on the Moon, astronauts' footprints could last for millions of years.

ja: カタツムリの中には、交尾のときに「恋矢（れんし）」という小さな針を相手に刺す種類がいる。
easy: Some snails shoot a small sharp 'love dart' into their partner.
std: Some land snails stab their mate with a calcium 'love dart' during courtship, which can increase their chances of fathering offspring.

ja: 1977年、電波望遠鏡が宇宙から72秒間の強い信号を受け取った。研究者が記録用紙に「Wow!」と書いたため「Wow!シグナル」と呼ばれ、正体は今も分かっていない。
easy: In 1977, a radio telescope picked up a strong signal from space. A scientist wrote 'Wow!' next to it. No one knows what it was.
std: In 1977 the Big Ear radio telescope recorded a strong 72-second signal; an astronomer wrote 'Wow!' on the printout, and its source remains unknown.

ja: エスペラントは1887年にザメンホフが作った人工言語。国どうしの理解のために考えられ、最も広く話されている人工言語になった。
easy: Esperanto is a language made by one man in 1887. He wanted people from different countries to understand each other.
std: Esperanto, created by L. L. Zamenhof in 1887 to promote international understanding, is the most widely spoken constructed language.
